course.title: Hair Colouring
course.tagline: Colour hair with confidence: dyes, highlights, balayage and colour care.

days.title: Welcome to Hair Colouring
days.goal: By the end of today you can explain and practise: Your kit is dye, developer, bowls, brushes, foils, gloves, clips and a cape.

video.title: Step by Step Colouring White and Grey Hair to Black Using Henna-Indigo Powder

steps: Get your tools ready: colour bowl and brush, developer and foils.
Watch the video. It explains the main point in simple steps: Gloves must be worn for every colour service.
Your kit is dye, developer (the liquid mixed with dye), bowls, brushes, foils, gloves, clips and a cape. Go slowly. Practise on a model or a practice head.
Do the same move three times. Check your work in a mirror or a photo after each try.
Write down what went well, what was hard, and one thing to do better tomorrow.
days.task: Practise welcome to hair colouring on a model or a practice head. Your kit is dye, developer (the liquid mixed with dye), bowls, brushes, foils, gloves, clips and a cape. Take a photo of your work.
days.challenge: Do welcome to hair colouring two times today. Make the second try neater than the first.

quiz.q: Which of these is true about hair colouring?
options: Gloves are only needed for dark colours.
Gloves must be worn for every colour service.
Bare hands are best for every colour service.
Gloves should never be worn when handling dye.
quiz.explain: Gloves must be worn for every colour service.

quiz.q: What do you use to mix and paint colour onto the hair?
options: developer
foils
colour bowl and brush
gloves
quiz.explain: A colour bowl and brush mix and paint colour onto the hair.

quiz.q: What should you always do when colouring hair?
options: colour hair without doing a patch test
handle dye with bare hands
put colour on a sore or cut scalp
do a patch test 48 hours before colouring
quiz.explain: You should always do a patch test 48 hours before colouring.

days.title: Colour Theory Basics
days.goal: By the end of today you can explain and practise: Learn the colour wheel: warm, cool and neutral tones, and how they cancel each other.

video.title: How to Dye Men's Gray Beard and Mustache to Black Naturally Using Henna and Indigo

steps: Get your tools ready: colour bowl and brush, developer and foils.
Watch the video. It explains the main point in simple steps: Purple cancels yellow tones in hair.
Learn the colour wheel: warm, cool and neutral tones, and how they cancel each other. Go slowly. Practise on a model or a practice head.
Do the same move three times. Check your work in a mirror or a photo after each try.
Write down what went well, what was hard, and one thing to do better tomorrow.
days.task: Practise colour theory basics on a model or a practice head. Learn the colour wheel: warm, cool and neutral tones, and how they cancel each other. Take a photo of your work.
days.challenge: Do colour theory basics two times today. Make the second try neater than the first.

quiz.q: Which of these is true about colour theory basics?
options: Purple adds more yellow tones to hair.
Yellow cancels purple tones in hair.
Purple cancels yellow tones in hair.
Purple has no effect on yellow tones.
quiz.explain: Purple cancels yellow tones in hair.

quiz.q: Which liquid do you mix with dye to make the colour work?
options: foils
gloves
colour bowl and brush
developer
quiz.explain: Developer is the liquid mixed with dye to make the colour work.

quiz.q: What should you always do when colouring hair?
options: always wear gloves when handling dye

put colour on a sore or cut scalp
leave dye on far longer than the time says
quiz.explain: Always wear gloves when handling dye.
